clues.clue: Lower Manhattan's CB1 holds this street where the original Dutch defensive wall gave the financial district its name.
clues.reveal: Wall Street (CB1). Named for an actual wall the Dutch built across lower Manhattan in the 1650s; now the heart of the financial district.

clues.clue: This Lower East Side institution and immigrant gateway gave CB3 generations of new New Yorkers.
clues.reveal: Lower East Side (CB3). One of the most densely settled immigrant neighborhoods in America, remembered today at the Tenement Museum.

clues.clue: CB2's bohemian neighborhood, a Dutch 'Noortwyck,' became the heart of 20th-century counterculture.
clues.reveal: Greenwich Village (CB2). A Dutch farming hamlet that became the city's bohemian and artistic center, home to Washington Square Park.

clues.clue: CB10's neighborhood, a Dutch village named 'Nieuw Haarlem' in 1658, sparked a 1920s cultural Renaissance.
clues.reveal: Harlem (CB10). Founded as the Dutch village of Nieuw Haarlem in 1658; epicenter of the 1920s Harlem Renaissance.

clues.clue: CB11's East Harlem became home to the city's largest Puerto Rican community, earning this Spanish nickname.
clues.reveal: El Barrio (CB11, East Harlem). Long the heart of the city's Puerto Rican community, also known as Spanish Harlem.

clues.clue: CB12's northern tip neighborhood shares its name with a fort and the Cloisters museum.
clues.reveal: Washington Heights (CB12). Named for the Revolutionary-era Fort Washington; home to the Cloisters and a large Dominican community.

clues.clue: CB5's crossroads, renamed in 1904 for a newspaper that moved there, is the 'Crossroads of the World.'
clues.reveal: Times Square (CB5). Formerly Longacre Square, renamed in 1904 after The New York Times built its tower there.

clues.clue: Completed in 1931 in CB5, this was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.
clues.reveal: Empire State Building (CB5). Finished in 1931; held the title of world's tallest building until 1970.

clues.clue: CB6's East Side complex, opened in 1952 on former slaughterhouse land, hosts the world's diplomats.
clues.reveal: United Nations (CB6). The UN headquarters opened in 1952 on the East River, on land once occupied by slaughterhouses.

clues.clue: Manhattan is coextensive with this New York County, the most densely populated county in the United States.
clues.reveal: New York County. Manhattan is coextensive with New York County, the most densely populated county in the U.S.

clues.clue: Designed by Olmsted and Vaux and opened in 1858, this 843-acre green space sits in the middle of the island.
clues.reveal: Central Park. The 843-acre park by Olmsted and Vaux opened in 1858, built on land that included the Black settlement of Seneca Village.

clues.clue: The island's name comes from a Lenape word generally said to mean 'island of' these.
clues.reveal: Hills. 'Manhattan' derives from the Lenape Mannahatta, commonly translated as 'island of many hills.'
